sections.h2: Where is Riverhead, and how big is the town?
sections.html:
Riverhead is a town at the eastern end of Suffolk County, where the North Fork meets the mouth of the Peconic River. The town covers 201.3 square miles, but only 67.4 of those are land, because about two thirds of the area is water.

Within the town sit the hamlets of Aquebogue, Baiting Hollow, Calverton, Jamesport, Northville, Wading River and the downtown hamlet of Riverhead itself, plus parts of Laurel and Manorville. Sellers should know which hamlet an address belongs to, because it decides the school district, the library district and the fire district on the tax bill.

The town had 35,902 people in 2020 and is estimated at 36,394 for July 2025. The town sits 76 miles northeast of New York City, and the Census Bureau puts the average commute to work at 27.5 minutes.

sections.h2: How did Riverhead become the Suffolk County seat?
sections.html:
The hamlet of Riverhead has been the Suffolk County seat since 1727, and the town itself was carved out of Southold by the state legislature in a bill passed on March 13, 1792. Residents of Southold's western end had complained that the town was too long for them to reach town meetings.

The land was first bought from the Algonquian-speaking Native Americans and the Shinnecock Indian Nation in 1649. In the early 1900s a wave of Polish immigrants settled here, and the Polish Town area downtown still hosts an annual fair. Most county offices moved west to Hauppauge in the 1960s, though courts and the Suffolk County Comptroller still keep Riverhead addresses.

Because settlement here is so old, a sale can turn on the paperwork behind the house: certificates of occupancy, permits for additions, and septic records. Gather those before you accept any offer.

sections.h2: What do Riverhead homes cost, and who owns them?
sections.html:
In the Census Bureau's 2020-2024 survey, a typical Riverhead house is valued at $486,600, and owners occupy 79.8 percent of homes. Tenants pay $1,974 a month, and the household in the middle of the income range takes in $94,249.

  • 14,202 households with 2.48 people apiece
  • Seniors make up 28.8 percent of the population, against 15.4 percent under 18
  • Only about 9 in 100 residents had a different address a year earlier
  • Carrying a house costs $2,944 a month with a mortgage and $1,364 without one

Few people move, and many owners are past 65, so plenty of Riverhead houses have been held for decades. Heirs and owners ready to downsize are the usual sellers who want a quick, simple close.

sections.h2: What do the roads, the railroad and the local economy mean for a Riverhead sale?
sections.html:
The Long Island Expressway ends in Calverton, inside Riverhead, which makes the town the end of that highway. New York Route 25, County Routes 58 and 105 and Sound Avenue carry local traffic. The Long Island Rail Road's Main Line has one station in town, in the hamlet of Riverhead, and Suffolk County Transit and Hampton Jitney buses also serve the town.

Riverhead is described as the agricultural center of Long Island: 20,000 of the island's roughly 35,000 acres of farmland lie inside the town. Census business data for 2022 lists $2.47 billion in retail sales and $607 million in medical and social-service revenue, so shopping and health care sit beside farming in the local economy.

Access and acreage change how a house is priced. A property near the expressway or the rail station, a lot with usable farmland and a house in a Sound-side hamlet like Wading River can each be valued differently.

sections.h2: Do weather and water matter when selling a house in Riverhead?
sections.html:
Yes, because so much of the town is shoreline. The town has Long Island Sound to the north, the Peconic River and bays, and four beaches that stay open all year. The weather station at the Riverhead Research Farm logs 47.22 inches of precipitation in a normal year and has recorded 100 degrees, so basements, roofs and sump pumps all get tested.

The disclosure form printed in Real Property Law section 462 asks sellers about floodplains, flood insurance, past flood claims, water in the basement, fuel tanks and septic age. A seller who skips delivery before the buyer signs a contract owes the buyer a $500 credit against the price, according to the Department of State's copy. Answer from what you actually know and attach any radon, septic or mold reports you have.

sections.h2: What rental permit rules apply to a Riverhead house with tenants?
sections.html:
Town Code Chapter 263 requires an owner to get a rental permit before renting out a dwelling, and the permit does not pass to a new owner. The Code Enforcement Division at 4 West Second Street handles applications, and the town now runs them through an online portal.

The town's own summary of Chapter 263 lists these points:

  • A permit applies to the whole premises, and a multi-family house needs one for each rented unit.
  • Rentals of 29 days or less are prohibited as transient rentals.
  • A new owner must register the property within 30 days of closing of title.
  • First offenses carry fines of $250 to $1,000, and each additional week can count as a separate violation.

The same summary shows a $300 fee for a two-year permit, but the code enforcement page links a separate fee sheet, so confirm today's figure with the office. If your tenant moves out before closing, a lapsed permit is one more item a buyer's attorney may raise.

sections.h2: When do Riverhead tax bills come due, and how does a sale affect them?
sections.html:
Riverhead's Receiver of Taxes mails one bill in mid-December and splits it into two halves, due about January 10 and May 31. A weekend due date slides to Monday, which is why the 2025-26 halves landed on January 12 and June 1. The receiver collects town, county, school, fire and special district taxes together.

Taxes unpaid after June 1 are paid to the Suffolk County Comptroller, and unpaid parcels go to the county tax lien sale in November or December. The tax year runs December 1 to November 30. After a sale, the receiver's page asks the owner to report the transfer to the office, and a bill can keep showing the former owner for up to six months. A buyer who does not qualify for the seller's exemptions will see a "pro-rata" charge, so ask the closing attorney to prorate with that in mind.

sections.h2: What does recording a Riverhead deed involve?
sections.html:
Deeds for Riverhead properties are recorded with the Suffolk County Clerk. The clerk's deed schedule lists a base cost of $245 plus $5 for each page, and the filing must include the state transfer tax form TP-584 and the real property transfer report.

The clerk's page also states that transfer tax applies to any conveyance over $500, at two dollars for every $500, or part of $500, paid for the property. Residential sales at $1,000,000 or more also owe the mansion tax, payable by cash or certified check to the Suffolk County Clerk. For the tax map number, the clerk's page sends you to the Town Assessor. Most sellers hand all of this to the closing attorney, but it helps to know that the recording is a separate step from the closing table.

sections.h2: Which sale route suits a Riverhead house that must move quickly?
sections.html:
Three paths are open: hire an agent, handle the sale alone, or sell to a cash buyer. Weigh them by repairs needed and how many weeks you can wait.

  • An agent listing reaches the most buyers, though repairs, showings and a buyer's loan approval all stretch the timeline.
  • Selling alone saves the commission, but pricing, the disclosure form and the contract are yours to manage.
  • A cash purchase suits a property with postponed repairs, rental permit trouble, an inherited title or a hard deadline. Get the figure in writing, then subtract what a listing would cost you in repairs and closing charges.

Whatever you pick, gather the rental permit, the latest tax bill, the disclosure statement and any septic or oil tank records first.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Riverhead house if it was rented without a permit?
faqs.a: Yes, but expect questions. Chapter 263 makes renting without a permit a violation, and the permit is not transferable, so a buyer must register within 30 days of closing. Ask Code Enforcement what it would take to get the file in order before you list.

faqs.q: Who do I pay Riverhead property taxes to?
faqs.a: Pay the Town of Riverhead Receiver of Taxes at 4 West Second Street until June 1, after which unpaid balances go to the Suffolk County Comptroller at 330 Center Drive in Riverhead. The receiver collects town, county, school and district taxes on one bill.

faqs.q: How do I find my Riverhead school district?
faqs.a: It depends on the hamlet. The receiver collects school taxes for four districts inside the town: Riverhead, Shoreham-Wading River, Mattituck-Cutchogue and Eastport South Manor. The district name is printed on your tax bill.

faqs.q: Does the seller or the buyer pay New York transfer tax?
faqs.a: The county clerk collects the tax with the deed, at two dollars per $500 on sales above $500. Your contract decides who pays, so have your attorney check that clause before you sign.

faqs.q: Where do I record the deed after closing in Riverhead?
faqs.a: File it with the Suffolk County Clerk, whose recording unit examines and records deeds and collects the fees and taxes. The clerk's office lists (631) 852-2000 as its contact number.
